title: 479. Convert a Number to Hexadecimal

examples.explanation: Negative values use 32-bit two's complement, so -1 becomes eight f digits.
Zero maps to a single zero digit.

hints: Handle zero as a special case returning a single zero character.
Treat the value as an unsigned 32-bit pattern so negatives wrap via two's complement.
Peel off 4-bit groups from the low end, mapping 0-15 to 0-9a-f, until nothing remains.
